solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Method of carrying almost half a ton, including rare minerals

indicators.note: including means one piece takes the other inside it
almost means the word falls one letter short of complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, so half of it is fifty

indicators.note: rare, like underdone meat, signals that the letters of minerals are left unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A haulier moves nearly fifty tons including some rare minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' (as in undercooked) is the anagram signal, making REMANSLI; 'including' sets it between FI and FT. 'Method of carrying' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireman's lift is the technique of carrying a person over one shoulder, used in rescues.

clue.text: Ship: arrangement of sails etc crushed by one's sinking?

indicators.note: crushed by means held inside, squeezed between the letters of another word

parts.note: sinking is one's doom, one's fate
a ship's rig is the arrangement of its masts, sails and rigging

explanation.surface: A ship's rigging is crushed as it goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed by' signals containment. Reading 'one's sinking' as fate is loose: going down is the doom that awaits a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship, once a sailing vessel and now an escort vessel.

clue.text: Entering difficult battle, a unit unfortunately in range

parts.note: rocky means difficult, as in a rocky patch

indicators.note: entering means going inside another word

parts.note: Mons is a Belgian town, scene of a First World War battle

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of a unit are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A military unit unluckily enters a hard fight within firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons, in Belgium, was the first British battle of 1914. 'unfortunately' gives UNTAI, which 'Entering' places in the battle's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rocky Mountains are the great mountain range of western North America.

clue.text: Get one's teeth into eminent expressionist

definitions.meaning: Edvard ..., the Norwegian painter of The Scream

explanation.surface: Tackle with relish a famous expressionist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Munch is both a verb for chewing noisily and the surname of the celebrated Norwegian Expressionist painter.

clue.text: Name foe, by implication, has smuggled in

indicators.note: has smuggled means one word carries the other hidden inside it

parts.note: a foe is no mate, not a friend

explanation.surface: An informer names an enemy who has smuggled goods into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by implication' warns that NO MATE is a description of a foe rather than a synonym; 'has smuggled' puts IN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to name them formally as a candidate or appointee.

clue.text: Symbol of goddess of love initially erected

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the letters are set upright, read from the bottom up
initially means take the opening letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A statue of the goddess of love was the first thing put up as an emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives OGOL from the first letters, and 'erected' turns them upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or design used as a company's identifying sign.

clue.text: Copy a brief selection of miscellaneous characters up into dossier

indicators.note: into means placed inside another word

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers

indicators.note: up in a down clue means these letters read upward, from the bottom

parts.note: misc is the short form of miscellaneous, a few of its characters

explanation.surface: Someone files a few stray characters into a dossier as a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' signals the standard short form of miscellaneous; 'up' turns it to CSIM, and 'into' places it with A inside the dossier.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile is an exact reproduction of a document or picture.

clue.text: Right-wing US pal organised debauched feast

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American right-winger arranges a wild party with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Walpurgis Night, the eve of May Day, is in folklore the witches' sabbath of revelry.

clue.text: Newspaper worker in routine procedure wrapping papers up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole is read from the bottom upward
wrapping means one word goes round the other

parts.note: rote is fixed routine, done by habit
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: A journalist goes through the routine of wrapping up newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' gives ROTIDE, and 'up' reads it bottom to top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the journalist who directs a newspaper's content.

clue.text: Native of South America once imprisoned?

definitions.meaning: a member of the Inca people of the Andes
read as two words, ..., and can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Was a former South American native locked up?
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an empire in Peru until the Spanish conquest; 'can' is American slang for jail.

clue.text: Quick fix, fantastic load of money saving corporation, finally

parts.note: magic means fantastic, wonderful

indicators.note: saving means keeping something inside

parts.note: a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A big corporation is saved by an astonishing cash injection, as a fast remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives N from corporation; 'saving' puts it inside WAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic wand is figuratively an instant solution to a problem.

clue.text: Whatever takes your fancy, many thin gassy drinks?

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Order whatever you like, even lots of weak fizzy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything means whatever thing one likes, with no restriction.

clue.text: Rogue beset by obstruction that's difficult to shift

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by another word

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'
an imp is a little rogue, a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A villain is hemmed in by a roadblock he cannot move.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the shellfish clings so firmly to rocks that it is notoriously hard to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish that clamps to rock, hence a byword for something that clings and won't budge.

clue.text: Hate stealing or wicked crime

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: enmity is hatred

explanation.surface: Is it hatred or theft that makes a crime evil?
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is an act of great wickedness, an outrage.

clue.text: User of device, a feature in film

indicators.note: in means set inside another word

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A gadget appears as a prop in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist is someone who operates a machine, such as a sewing machine.

clue.text: Newspaper copy

explanation.surface: A newspaper's reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid; to mirror something is to reflect or imitate it.

clue.text: Ruby fastener found in river

definitions.note: a ruby wedding anniversary is the fortieth, so ruby stands for the ordinal

indicators.note: found in means placed inside another word

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river
a tie fastens things together

explanation.surface: A jewelled clasp is recovered from a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on the convention that a ruby anniversary marks forty years. The Forth flows through Stirling into the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries take gem names, and the ruby anniversary is the fortieth year of marriage.

clue.text: Bully boys grown up perfect

parts.note: boys once grown up are men
ace means excellent, perfect

explanation.surface: Bully boys reach adulthood as model citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to threaten or intimidate them, as a bully does.

clue.text: Venom shown by nation over evacuation of Chile

parts.note: Mali is a West African nation

indicators.note: evacuation of means emptying the word, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A country's spite is shown as it pulls out of Chile.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spiteful ill will, figuratively venom.

clue.text: Lofty monarch hauling bags

indicators.note: bags means captures, holding something inside

parts.note: towing is hauling
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A haughty king drags luggage about.
explanation.definitionFit: Towering means very tall, soaring high.

clue.text: Old material put up, secure decoration

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means read upward, from the bottom

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of old cloth
to land is to secure, as a catch or a deal

explanation.surface: Old fabric is hung up and fixed as a festive ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath of flowers or leaves worn or hung as an adornment.

clue.text: Opening element, batting

parts.note: lead is a chemical element
in cricket, the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: An opening batsman is a key element when batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is an introduction or opening to something.

clue.text: Small shoe that's full of holes

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a trainer is a sports shoe

explanation.surface: A small sneaker that's riddled with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve, perforated to let liquid through.

clue.text: Adrift on the water

explanation.surface: Drifting on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally at sea means sailing offshore; figuratively it means bewildered or lost.

clue.text: Story that can be spun out?

explanation.surface: A tale that can be stretched out.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long tale, and also spun thread; to spin a yarn is to tell one.

clue.text: Frank finished off contender

parts.note: candid means frank
ate means consumed, finished off food

explanation.surface: Frank dispatched a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone competing for a post or prize, a contender.

clue.text: Little time to avoid damage to reputation for Greek character

indicators.note: to avoid means the letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Greek tries quickly to dodge disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Cold established, fed wild honey

indicators.note: fed means given something inside it

parts.note: started means set up, established

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A cold that has set in is treated with wild honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' sits at the start like the surface's ailment but is the definition. 'wild' gives ONYHE, which 'fed' puts after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony-hearted means unfeeling and cruel, emotionally cold.
